body.working_title: Admissibility of lagged SSOE models: replacing the per-lag eigenvalue check

body.text: Which criterion decides whether a pure additive lagged SSOE model (ADAM notation, components with different lags, including GUM) forgets its initial states, and how can it be computed efficiently inside the estimation loop?

Before this record was started, the agent ran unrecorded numpy checks (in a scratchpad, not in the repository) while designing the checker for issue openforecast-org/smooth#415 with the human. Those checks shaped the criterion and the hypotheses below. Their code was consolidated into .claude/research/eigenChecker and is re-run here as exploratory run(s), so that every number used later comes from a recorded run.

Prototype in numpy before the R/C++ implementation: the criterion is the invertibility of the MA polynomial theta(B) = det(I - D L(B)) of the model's ARIMA form, after cancelling the cyclotomic factors it shares with phi(B) = det(I - F L(B)), with coefficients from an inverse DFT and the decision from the step-down (Schur-Cohn) recursion.

body.statement: The per-lag eigenvalue check of smoothEigens() (eigenvalues of the diagonal blocks of D = F - g w', one block per lag) accepts lagged SSOE models that do not forget their initial states (some controllable and observable mode of the expanded discount matrix has |lambda| > 1): ETS(A,N,A) models with m = 4 or 12 on a grid of alpha and gamma in (0, 2), and GUM models with lags (1, 12) and random F, g, w.
body.question: Q1

body.statement: The per-lag eigenvalue check of smoothEigens() rejects some GUM models with lags (1, 12) that do forget their initial states (every controllable and observable mode of the expanded discount matrix has |lambda| < 1).
body.question: Q1

body.statement: For additive ETS models (level, optional damped trend, up to two seasonal lags, optional constant, some persistence fixed at zero) and GUM models (identity or random transition), dividing theta(B) = det(I - D L(B)) and phi(B) = det(I - F L(B)) by the cyclotomic factors Phi_n (n dividing a lag) they share gives the same admissibility decision as the controllable and observable modes of the expanded discount matrix (PBH reference), and the same max |lambda| within 1e-6 on inadmissible models.
body.question: Q1

body.statement: The step-down (Schur-Cohn) recursion applied to the cancelled MA polynomial theta*(B) gives the same admissibility decision as the roots of theta*, for ETS and GUM models with polynomial degrees up to 366.
body.question: Q1

body.statement: For inadmissible models, bisection on r with the step-down test applied to theta*(B/r) gives max |lambda| within 1e-8 of the value from the roots of theta*.
body.question: Q1

body.text: The ETS(A,N,A) part of PL1 uses a fixed grid of alpha and gamma that does not depend on the seed, so it is the same grid as exploratory run RN3, whose result prompted H1. Only the GUM part of PL1 (200 models from seed 2026) is new data. For the ETS part the confirmatory run repeats a deterministic computation rather than testing on new data.

The PBH reference (pbh_max) and the cyclotomic cancellation share the lag-1 expansion code (expand) and the numpy/LAPACK eigenvalue routines, and were written by the same agent; the agreement in PL3 is not a check by an independent implementation.

Exploratory timings (RN2, numpy, one machine, degree 193): coefficients by inverse DFT 4.7 ms with a Python loop over 256 points, step-down test 0.007 ms, all roots by numpy companion eigenvalues 22 ms.

body.text: An independent checker agent (Claude Sonnet 5.5, given only the claimset and the scripts) reproduced the results of RN7-RN11 and RN2 and re-derived the formal claims. It reported: (1) the high-degree model set of PL4/PL5 reaches MA polynomial degrees up to 535 before cancellation, not 366 as written in PL4's design; (2) the step-down timing of RN2 was measured on an inadmissible polynomial on which the recursion stops at its first step, so it is not the cost of a full recursion; (3) the result labelled 'block-diagonal D, lags (1,12)' in RN2 comes from D = [[0.7, 0], [-0.1, 0.3]], which is lower-triangular, not block-diagonal.
The model set generated by the code named in the plan reached MA polynomial degrees up to 535 before cancellation (533 after), not up to 366 as the plan's design text states; the code ran unchanged.

Switch every caller of smoothEigens() in R and Python to the polynomial check (smoothEigensCpp now is it), as the human decided after the comparison with the derivation of the ADAM monograph; the temporary entry points are removed.

The derivation of the stability condition in Section 5.4 of the ADAM monograph (online version at openforecast.org/adam, eqs 5.20-5.22, identical in the book's source repository config-i1/adam) splits D into D_{m_i} = F_{m_i} - g_{m_i} w'_{m_i}; their sum is F - sum_i g_{m_i} w'_{m_i}, which differs from D = F - g w' by the cross terms g_{m_i} w'_{m_j}, i != j. The non-zero eigenvalues of D_{m_i} are those of the diagonal block of D for the lag m_i, which smoothEigensCpp() computed (and the earlier R code commented out in R/helper.R). An unrecorded scratchpad computation of the full recursion for ETS(A,N,A) prompted the recorded check that follows.

body.statement: For the same random ETS+ARIMA models, the criterion of Q1 applied to the whole model (the MA polynomial of the ARIMA form of the whole lagged SSOE after cyclotomic cancellation, with the AR polynomial of the ARIMA part stationary) gives the same admissibility decision as the PBH reference of the whole model on every model, and the same largest modulus within 1e-6 on the models both find inadmissible.
body.question: Q2

body.statement: For ETS+ARIMA models with a stationary AR polynomial, the polynomials theta and phi of the whole model share no non-cyclotomic factor with a root inside the unit circle: phi is the product of the ETS part's, whose roots are on the unit circle or are 1/phi of a damped trend (phi below one), and the stationary ARI polynomial, whose non-cyclotomic roots lie outside the circle. So the PBH reference (reachable and observable modes) and the cancelled MA polynomial decide the same forecastability here, unlike the GUM counterexample of NT14.

body.text: RN52 wrote its results and then crashed at exit (exit code -11), as RN51 did. The crash is in the Python build of smooth, not in the study's code: any process that calls smooth_eigens() on a model whose MA polynomial has degree 16 or more (lags summing to 16 or more, e.g. 24 and 168) crashes at exit, when the static caches of src/headers/eigenCalc.h (roots of unity, cyclotomic polynomials, the last phi) are destroyed and their Armadillo memory, more than 16 elements and so on the heap, is freed through numpy's allocator (carma), which is gone by then (gdb: PyDataMem_FREE from __run_exit_handlers). The results written before the exit are not affected. The caches are now never destroyed; R, which allocates through R, was not affected.

body.notes: Re-derived and reran. Formal: for ADAM's ARIMA part F = -a 1', g = ma - a, w = 1 (a = ari coefficients per state lag), so phi = det(I + 1' L a) = ari polynomial and D = F - g w' = -ma 1', theta = ma polynomial; checked numerically on 57 and 238 matrices built by adam() itself (AC3.RN3, AC3.RN11: max abs gap of det(I-FL) and det(I-DL) to ari and ma polynomials 1.4e-14). Cross terms: ETS(A,N,N) alpha=1.9 + MA(1) theta=0.1 has whole theta = 1 + B - 0.1 B^2 (exact fractions), the product of the parts' thetas is 1 + B + 0.09 B^2, smallest root modulus 0.916 against 1.111 (AC3.RN3), so the parts-apart check accepts a model that does not forget its states (package modulus 1.0916 whole, 0.9 ETS part alone). Reproduction with new seeds, script unchanged: seed 11 n=200 (AC3.RN1): split check differs from PBH on 65/200 ETS+ARIMA and 71/200 ETS+SARIMA; seed 12 n=200 (AC3.RN2): 67/200 and 58/200; author's RN49 166/500 and 159/500; all far above the 5% rule (25/500). Both directions occur (AC3.RN1: split accepts and PBH rejects 42 and 64; reverse 23 and 7). Review of ets_arima.py: the split baseline matches the old admissible branch of adam_bounds_checker (git 094b76f4~1: smoothEigens on ETS/constant/regressors apart, AR and MA reflections for the ARIMA); generators, AR via reflection coefficients, over-differencing, structure check against adam() (30 models, max gap 4.9e-15, AC3.RN1) are correct. Caveats, not disputes: (1) the percentage depends on the generator (alpha up to 1.9, MA reflection up to 1.5, 15% over-differenced by design), so '>5%' says the parts-apart check is wrong on a non-negligible share of such models, not on real fits; (2) over-differenced MA unit roots that cancel with a difference make the split check reject models PBH accepts, a mechanism other than the ETS-ARIMA cross terms (the cross-term direction alone is 104/500 and 128/500 in RN49 and still above 25); (3) RN49 and RN50 are the same command with the same results.json hash, so they are one data set tested under two plans; (4) the 'code changed after plan' flag is benign: git diff 397f255f..acb23120 touches only lab files.

Proved and tested. phi of the whole model is the product of the ETS part's (F block-diagonal): level and seasonals give Phi_n, n dividing the lag (roots on the unit circle), a damped trend adds 1/phi_damp (outside the circle for phi_damp < 1), the constant adds 1-B; ADAM's ARI polynomial is the ari polynomial (differences are cyclotomic, stationary AR roots strictly outside; AC3.RN3, AC3.RN11 verify phi = ari on adam() matrices to 1e-14). So phi has no root inside the circle and no non-cyclotomic root on it, hence shares no root with theta there; only cyclotomic factors can cancel on the circle. Independent argument for the equivalence with PBH: uncontrollable and unobservable modes of D have the eigenvalues of F (feedback and output injection leave them unchanged), which are all of modulus at most 1, so every eigenvalue of D above 1 is reachable and observable; at modulus 1 it is the cyclotomic cancellation that decides. Numerically, an exact oracle (Fraction determinants, exact gcd(theta, phi), which cancels any shared factor, not only cyclotomic) agrees with the cyclotomic-only cancellation on 1750 wider-generator models (AC3.RN4-RN10, 0 differences). Unstated preconditions to add: damped phi at most 1 (adam bounds it to [0,1]; phi above 1 puts a root of phi inside the circle) and the AR actually being checked for stationarity (not the case when the AR parameters are provided and not estimated, where the premise fails); for adaptive regressors (time-varying w) the assumption is not covered.

The shortcut is exact. Derivation: a constant or static regressor has F row e_x, g_x = 0, so row x of D is also e_x and expanding det(I - D L) along it gives theta_whole = theta_ARIMA (1 - B) and phi_whole = phi_ARIMA (1 - B) (checked on adam() matrices of plain, constant and static-regressor ARIMA, 295 models in total, max gap 1.4e-14, AC3.RN3, AC3.RN11). With every MA factor invertible theta_ARIMA has no root on or inside the circle, the (1 - B) factors cancel with phi, so theta* has all roots outside; this holds whether or not the AR is stationary. Code: in R (adam_bounds_checker in R/utils-adam.R and ssarima in R/adam-ssarima.R) and Python (cost_functions.py) the whole check is skipped only when no ETS, no adaptive regressors, arima_model true and ma_reflection < 1, otherwise it runs, so an MA root that cancels with a difference is still accepted (reflection >= 1 goes to the whole check). maReflection is the factor-by-factor Schur-Cohn value, below 1 exactly when every factor is invertible. Tests (mine, the author has no recorded run of the shortcut: RN53 only used ets_model=True and predates b4a10cc6; RN55/RN56 are timing): on 238 adam()-built pure ARIMA models (plain 80, constant 80, static regressor 78; AC3.RN11) 136 have all MA roots outside the circle and smooth_eigens rejects 0 of them; the real R adam_bounds_checker() with etsModel FALSE (AC3.RN12) gives a penalty on 0 of the 136 and its decision equals the forced whole-model check on all 102 non-invertible ones (20 of them are accepted, the cancelling roots). body.text: Response to the caveats of AC3's checks (AC3.CK1, CK4-CK7): (1) the package decides an MA root exactly on the unit circle that does not cancel by roundoff, as the check of Q1 did (AC3.RN4, RN9, RN10, RN13); the random models of PL7-PL9 have none, so H9 holds for models away from the boundary, and the claimset says so; changing the decision rule of the package is left to the human. (2) The PBH reference is not exact for a repeated unit root (AC3.RN9); the generators of PL7-PL9 have none; stated as a limitation of the reference. (3) The share of disagreements of H7 depends on the generator, and part of the models rejected by the parts apart and accepted by the reference are over-differenced; the models accepted by the parts apart and rejected by the reference alone (104 and 128 of 500 in RN49) exceed the threshold of PL7; RN49 and RN50 are the same command and data, tested under two plans. (4) The shortcut of DC6 is tested only by AC3.RN11 and AC3.RN12.

body.text: Two changes to the bounds checkers after review: (1) a model is admissible only when the value of smoothEigens() is at most 1 - 1e-10 (it was 1 + 1e-50 in the checkers of adam(), ssarima(), ces(), gum(), and 1 + 1e-10 in eigenValues() of confint() and reapply(), sim.gum() and their Python counterparts), so that an MA root on the unit circle that does not cancel is rejected rather than decided by rounding: the three models of the checker with values from 0.99999999999709 to 0.9999999999999993 (AC3.RN4, RN9, RN10) are above the margin; the human agreed. (2) For a pure ARIMA (no ETS, no adaptive regressors), a stationary AR leaves the MA to the check of the whole model, which runs only when an estimated MA factor is not invertible, and a rejected model keeps the penalty of its MA factors, 1e100 times their largest reflection coefficient, as before the change: with the root modulus as penalty, auto.adam() on BJsales stopped at another point of the same ARIMA(2,1,2) with drift (log-likelihood -254.083203 against -254.083151), failing a test of the package; with the old penalty the estimates of pure ARIMA are those before the change except where an MA root cancels with a difference.
